_meta.description: Operator-curated state primary (and primary-runoff) election dates for U.S. federal elections. Consumed by scripts/build_election_calendar.py, which merges these rows with the statutory federal general-election date to publish docs/data/election_calendar.json (issue #23, epic #16).
_meta.why_curated: Per issue #23 correctness beats automation: a wrong primary date is worse than a missing one. Primary dates are announced far ahead and rarely move, so a small hand-verified file in-repo is safer than scraping. Each row carries its own `source` so provenance travels with the date and stays auditable.
_meta.update_cadence: Reviewed and extended once per even-year federal cycle (and whenever a state moves its primary). Verify every date against the state's Secretary of State / election-authority page before adding it. Rows failing validation (unparseable date, unknown state, non-even election_year) are dropped by the builder with a warning rather than published.

schema.date: ISO-8601 calendar date YYYY-MM-DD in the state's jurisdiction
schema.election_year: even-numbered federal cycle year the primary feeds into
schema.source: human-readable attribution for this specific date

_meta.verification_status: SEED — the entries below are statutorily-fixed 2026 primary dates; an operator must re-confirm each against the official state source before the first live publish, and add the remaining states.

primaries.source: Texas Election Code §41.007 (first Tuesday in March in even years)
Indiana Code §3-10-1-3 (first Tuesday after first Monday in May of even years)
Ohio Rev. Code §3501.01 (first Tuesday after first Monday in May)
Nebraska Rev. Stat. §32-401 (second Tuesday in May of even years)
West Virginia Code §3-5-1 (second Tuesday in May)
Oregon Rev. Stat. §254.056 (third Tuesday in May of even years)
25 Pa. Stat. §2753 (third Tuesday in May in even years)
